vulnerabilities.title: Private message attachments are accessible without authentication
vulnerabilities.evidence:
PATH=/uploads/messages/20261011-783b9b6608b97051c19ee752.txt
HTTP_STATUS=200
CONTENT_TYPE=text/plain; charset=UTF-8
BODY=Fictional Chapter 6 attachment evidence.
vulnerabilities.impact: Anyone who learns or receives the randomized URL can download a file from a supposedly private conversation. Random names reduce guessing but are not authorization.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Store message files outside public/, expose a download controller that requires login and verifies sender/receiver ownership, set Content-Disposition and nosniff, and migrate existing attachments.

vulnerabilities.title: No Content-Security-Policy header is set
vulnerabilities.evidence: public/index.php:5-6 sets nosniff and SAMEORIGIN, but no Content-Security-Policy header was found.
vulnerabilities.impact: Existing output escaping passed, but a future injection defect would have fewer browser-side containment controls.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Deploy a nonce- or hash-based CSP after inventorying inline scripts/styles; start with Report-Only.

vulnerabilities.title: HSTS is not configured in application code
vulnerabilities.evidence: No Strict-Transport-Security header was found. Local tests used HTTP by design.
vulnerabilities.impact: A production deployment must rely on the reverse proxy/web server for HTTPS enforcement and HSTS.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: At the production proxy, redirect HTTP to HTTPS and enable HSTS only after HTTPS is correct for all subdomains.

limitations: The HTTP tests ran on PHP 8.1.25's built-in development server and a local MySQL database; PERF-001 is a safe response-time sample, not a production capacity or concurrent load test.
Google OAuth, SMTP delivery, Stripe test mode, Firefox, mobile viewports, and controlled concurrency were not executed. They remain in the proposed table.
All AI provider credentials were blank. AI-002 tested MANBAR's deterministic local rules fallback, not Gemini/Groq/OpenAI quality or availability.
PAY-001 used MANBAR's internal demonstration-payment flow. No payment network was contacted and no real money moved.
Chrome and Edge checks verified public login rendering and retained screenshots; authenticated cross-browser workflows were not automated.
A 25 MB course-material upload boundary was verified by code inspection but was not uploaded during this run to avoid unnecessary disk consumption; it is explicitly proposed below.

proposed_tests.input_values: Valid allowlisted file at exactly 26,214,400 bytes and another at 26,214,401 bytes; mismatched extension/MIME pair
proposed_tests.expected_output: Exact 25 MB file is stored outside public root; 25 MB + 1 and MIME mismatch are rejected with no database row/file residue
proposed_tests.verification_procedure: On a disposable clone, POST multipart files to the authenticated course/material and service portfolio endpoints; inspect HTTP messages, material/service_files rows, and storage/course_files or storage/service_files.
proposed_tests.reason_not_executed: The 25 MB rule was confirmed statically; large binary boundary execution was omitted to keep the evidence run lightweight.
